description: Catalog all X-MEM files; names + register counts printed to PRINT buffer
example: XEQ "EMDIR" -> prints file list e.g. PROG1 P 20 / DATA1 D 100
notes: Output goes to print_buffer; drain via PRA/PRX. Empty X-MEM prints nothing.

description: Return number of available X-MEM registers in X
example: XEQ "EMROOM" -> X = 600 (600 registers free in a fresh X-MEM)
notes: Result in X; total capacity is 600 registers, decreasing by (entry + registers) per stored file.

description: Save current program to X-MEM file named by ALPHA register
example: "MYPROG" ALPHA, XEQ "SAVEP" -> program stored as MYPROG in X-MEM
notes: ALPHA must hold the filename (1-6 chars). Round-trip: SAVEP then GETP restores exact program.

description: Load program from X-MEM file named by ALPHA into current program memory
example: "MYPROG" ALPHA, XEQ "GETP" -> program memory replaced with MYPROG
notes: ALPHA must hold the filename. Existing program memory is overwritten.

description: Save all currently-allocated data registers to X-MEM file named by ALPHA register
example: "REGS" ALPHA, XEQ "SAVED" -> current data registers stored in X-MEM file REGS
notes: Saves the data-register set as currently sized by SIZE. Use GETD to restore. Pairs with GETD for register transfer.

description: Load all data registers from X-MEM file named by ALPHA register
example: "REGS" ALPHA, XEQ "GETD" -> data registers restored from X-MEM file REGS
notes: Loads the saved data-register set from a data file. Existing registers are overwritten.

description: Recall register N (index from X) of the active X-MEM data file; pushes its value onto X
example: 5, XEQ "EMREG" -> X = value of register 5 in the active X-MEM data file
notes: N is taken from X (integer truncation). The active file is set by the most recent SAVED/GETD/SAVERX. Errors if no active data file or N is out of range.

description: Store Y into register N (index from X) of the active X-MEM data file
example: 42 ENTER 5, XEQ "SAVERX" -> register 5 of the active data file set to 42 (X=index, Y=value)
notes: X holds the register index, Y holds the value. The active file is set by the most recent SAVED/GETD. Errors if no active data file or index out of range.
